newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 5.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) decreased its estimate for economic growth this year from 4.5 percent to 3.2 percent. The CSU added that the trade deficit should not exceed 200 billion crowns. Yearly inflation this year should not be higher than last year's 8.8 percent.

- A new investment study from the Institute of International Finance says that slow reforms and unresolved problems in the banking sector and on the capital market had a larger impact on the Czech economy than monetary policy.

- During the first quarter of this year, demand for electricity plummeted. Year-on-year it declined on average by 5.5 percent, by 8.7 percent for large clients. CEZ's profits after taxes decreased by 30 percent.
- During the first quarter of this year, the Czech trade surplus with CEFTA countries declined by one-fourth to 5.6 billion crowns, according to the Czech Statistical Bureau.

- According to preliminary reports, Skoda Praha a.s. managed to obtain an order to supply tubular systems for a heating power plant on which construction is beginning in Ajum Mussa, Egypt, valued at approximately $40 million.
- Centroprojekt Zlin a.s. had gross turnover last year of 179 million crowns, an increase of 50 percent over 1995.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The chairman of the doctors' union and the initiatior of the strike in Motol Hospital, David Rath, presented information to the Health Ministry on Friday, on the basis of which the doctors call for certain members of the hospital's management to resign.
- During the first quarter of this year, the department store Kotva had losses of 8.5 million crowns and its turnover reached 290.8 million crowns.
- Of about 60 strategic state-owned businesses, about one third should be privatised this year. The state wants primarily to get rid of companies of which it has already lost control.

PRAVO - Privatisation of the state's share in Investicni a Postovni Banka should be put on hold until the case of two members of its management is resolved, according to cabinet Vice-chairman Josef Lux.
- More than 75 percent of Czechs have already heard of the Internet, 45 percent have heard of it and are not so interested, and every 10th Czech citizen has practical experience with the Internet.

- The Slovak Airport Administration is allowing employees of Slovak Air Services s.r.o., a subsidiary of Czech Airlines (CSA), to continue their operations at Bratislava airport in May. Therefore, CSA will not cancel its flights to Bratislava.
- On May 31, another 509 shares will be delisted from the Prague Stock Exchange. The total number of shares delisted this year will reach 1,001.
- The government budget deficit increased in April and reached 11.98 billion crowns at the end of the month.

LIDOVE NOVINY - During a demonstration in front of the Interior Ministry in Prague, police arrested 12 people out of 200 demonstrators commemorating the raid on the rock club Propast. Eight policemen were wounded during Saturday's demonstration.
- Health Minister Jan Strasky apparently presented a secret list of businesses which have not paid health insurance.
- Beginning today, branches of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka will issue advantageous credits for energy from the fund PHARE.

- The turnover of Jawa Divisov a.s. was 76 million crowns last year, and its audited profits were 8.8 million crowns. In comparison to 1993, when Jawa was state-owned, its output increased 2.4 times, and its turnover increased yearly by 33 percent on average.
